items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: I mean, you know Miles certainly influenced me too.

ctx.x: Oh it surprises a million people. It even surprises me sometimes, but I’m constantly hearing that guy. I got to know him in his later years. I met him a few times when I was a kid but the thing that appealed to me was his simplicity. And I certainly don’t play simple

all the time. But there’s a certain lyrical simplicity that he has that makes me play a certain way. And not that he was the only guy — I mean, you know Miles certainly influenced me too. But Paul is a saxophone player, being the first — they say you never forget your first love, you know? Like a woman or whatever. It’s like I don’t forget my first influence. And he just played some great things. His earlier records really knocked me out. In fact, my favorite album, just for the record, is “Dave Brubeck at…

Yeah, there was a certain sound to that group. I had an experience of just hearing “Take Five” one day on the car radio, and I said, “Man that’s it. What is that?” That kind of starts a whole process maybe of going from one thing to the next.
